oracle_kind: offline local synthetic fixture; no network transport; no repository program execution
written_before: fixture construction and before any candidate implementation exists
fixture_family: fleet report traversal needs an ancestor tree that is absent from the fleet object store

fixture_shape.lane: one commit 'round-1: work' by author kama-shokunin, author time 1000, path 'f'
fixture_shape.fleet_commit_F1: author time 2000, first add of .ufo/reports/round-1/kama.md, whose '## Landed changes' section cites the lane commit by its full 40-hex sha
fixture_shape.fleet_commit_F2: author time 2100, adds notes.txt; F2 is fleet HEAD
fixture_shape.report_bytes: read from the committed blob at fleet HEAD (F2), never from the worktree
fixture_shape.missing_object: the ROOT TREE of F1 is removed from the fleet object store (loose object file deleted); every other object, including HEAD's tree and the report blob, stays present
fixture_shape.canary: a local git repository used only as a transport detector; any lazy fetch would be observable there

rows.fixture: fleet promisor-marked AND F1 root tree absent
must_not: a guessed first-add cutoff (now, tip-only, or any value not established from present objects)
a defect list of any kind (no verdict may be emitted at all)
rows.rationale: The report's first-add cutoff is derived from a fleet history traversal that diffs the tree of every commit on the path. With F1's tree absent, that traversal cannot complete: the cutoff is unknown, and unknown is not absence. preregistration expected_after bullet 3: 'An unavailable required commit/tree/blob/report object: exit2 could-not-evaluate, never a clean or failed verdict.'
rows.frozen_base_note: the r23 base also exits 2, but for the wrong reason: the blanket promisor-metadata refusal in check_history_repo ('partial clone (remote.origin.promisor)'), not for the missing object. The row is therefore a no-harm row for the repair: the exit code must not move, the justification must.

rows.fixture: identical to MFT-1 but with no promisor metadata at all (plain local fleet, F1 root tree absent)
rows.rationale: Availability, not metadata, decides. MFT-1 and MFT-2 differ only in the promisor configuration and must reach the same outcome; the pair shows the repair is driven by object availability. A candidate that refuses MFT-1 for metadata reasons but answers MFT-2 (or vice versa) has not implemented the preregistered policy.

rows.fixture: identical to MFT-1 but every object present (no deletion); the same promisor metadata
must_not: exit 2 (the r23 blanket refusal: this is the operability harm r24 repairs)
exit 1 (no defect exists in this fixture: the lane commit is cited)
rows.rationale: preregistration expected_after bullet 1: 'Complete local promisor-marked lane and fleet clones with valid cited commits: exact same substantive clean/failed findings as otherwise identical full clones, not exit2.' The pair MFT-1/MFT-3 is the minimal discriminator between 'marked' and 'incomplete'.
rows.frozen_base_note: known r23 harm, recorded as evidence, not as an acceptance criterion for the frozen arm

rows.fixture: identical to MFT-3 without promisor metadata
rows.rationale: Soundness of the fixture itself: the same objects audited through an ordinary local fleet give a clean verdict, so MFT-3's exit 2 can only come from the promisor metadata, never from the fixture shape.

premise_checks: F1 root tree object is absent from the fleet object store (cat-file -e fails)
fleet HEAD tree and the report blob are present (git show HEAD:<report> succeeds)

git log --diff-filter=A --format=%at -- <report> does not complete in the marked repository under --no-lazy-fetch: the ancestor tree is genuinely NEEDED by the report traversal (otherwise the row would be vacuous)
the canary repository is a real local git repository before the audit run and is unchanged afterwards
not_claimed: the exact wording of the candidate's refusal message
that any particular closure-checking git command is used
any behavior of live serving or of the promisor transport itself
